messages:
olivia: heads-up — Acme just asked for a migration path from prompt->messages + guaranteed system-role pinning. they want function calls + strict JSON schema outputs. can we scope this for next quarter?

devon: high level — we can do a dual-shape endpoint (messages as canonical, prompt alias for compat). big work is SDK changes, streaming compatibility, and function-calling plumbing across hosted/dedicated/private.

ben: what are the non-negotiables from the customer? clarity helps prioritize.

mike (solutions): Acme asks: 1) ability to lock a system message so teammates can't override it on dedicated accounts; 2) function calling with enforced response schema (we must reject/flag non-conformant model outputs); 3) low-latency streaming for interactive UI.

olivia:+1 to those. product asks: launch gated on docs, SDKs, migration guide, and evaluation showing no >1% delta in our hallucination/regression evals for the default assistant persona.

sara: for the eval metric — we should be explicit: regression = relative increase in hallucination rate on core prompt set. threshold = 1% absolute? or 10% relative? I vote absolute 1% to be conservative.

devon: implementation notes: proposal = keep messages array as primary. support a top-level prompt string as shorthand mapped to messages: [{role: "user", content: prompt}]. system role rules: only one system entry allowed; we enforce server-side when present (dedicated/private: tenant-configurable lockedSystemMessage).

devon: function calling shape: we follow pattern similar to existing function-call APIs: functions: [{name, description, parameters: JSONSchema}], function_call: "auto" | {name}. model returns either a normal assistant message or a function_call object. example: 
```json
{
  "messages": [{"role":"system","content":"You are an assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"get me today's weather"}],
  "functions": [{"name":"getWeather","description":"returns weather","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"city":{"type":"string"}},"required":["city"]}}],
  "function_call":"auto"
}
```

mike (solutions): and how do we handle schema enforcement? Acme wants us to actively validate outputs and surface failures.

devon: runtime will attempt to coerce/format model outputs into the JSON schema. if coercion fails, we return a structured error alongside the partial assistant text and increment a telemetry counter. default policy = FAIL_FAST for enterprise tenants (error + code 422). Hosted default = best-effort (return assistant text + warning header).

ben: rollout plan idea: 1) implement dual-shape parsing + locked system message config; 2) add function-calling plumbing + schema validator library; 3) SDKs + migration guide; 4) canary (5% traffic hosted + one dedicated customer); 5) monitor eval/regression metrics for two weeks, then expand.

olivia: launch criteria checklist (proposal):
- API supports messages + prompt alias (parsing tested)
- System message locking implemented for Dedicated/Private and honored on Hosted via tenant settings
- Function calling implemented and parameters schema supported
- Schema validation behavior documented and configurable per-tenant
- SDKs (python/js) shipping with examples and migration helpers
- Migration guide + compatibility shim in console for legacy apps
- Evals: hallucination delta <= 1% absolute across core sets
- Perf: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms for 32-token responses on default model in hosted region
- Observability: request-level function_call traces, schema validation counters, migration warnings surfaced in console
- Rollback plan and automated fallback to legacy prompt-only endpoint

devon: engineering asks: we need 4 weeks for core runtime + 2 weeks for SDKs/docs + 1 week for canary ops. resource ask: 1 infra eng, 1 runtime eng, 1 SDK, 0.5 QA.

sara: we should add model / quantization matrix — some quantized variants change tokenization and can affect function-calling parsing. add a compatibility test matrix in CI.

mike (solutions): customer-facing: provide an interview-style migration checklist for solutions engineers. include examples of lockedSystemMessage config, example requests, and failure modes.

ben: prioritization: given capacity, do we do this or ship embeddings + rerank improvements first? embeddings/rerank has clear usage spikes from search teams.

olivia: prioritization decision — tie to revenue and risk. Acme is a potential Dedicated long-term commit. function-calling + schema + locked system message is high enterprise convert. embeddings/rerank is high volume but lower immediate enterprise conversion. recommend we fast-track chat-shape + function-calls for enterprise, schedule embeddings next sprint.

devon: to reduce scope, optional items we can cut from v1: per-tenant complex policy UI and advanced console shims. keep migration shim CLI + docs for v1.

olivia: agree. next actions: @devon open runtime ticket with acceptance criteria (include sample requests + schema), @ben file product PRD and migration guide stub, @sara add compatibility tests to shared CI matrix, @mike prepare customer-facing migration checklist. tag me once done and we schedule a backlog grooming to approve timeline. :raised_hands: 

deploy-bot: scheduled canary rollout job queued (canary-percent=5, target=hosted-us-west-2) — run when engineering gives green.

mike (solutions): noted. I'll draft the Acme proposal + example code snippets; want to align on the lockedSystemMessage API shape.

devon: quick sketch for locked system API (internal):
```json
POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/system_message_lock
{ "lockedSystemMessage": "<content>", "enforced": true }
```
response 200 with the effective locked message.

olivia: solid. thanks team — let's sync in the sprint planning meeting tomorrow to lock dates.
